text:
alex: ops — looks like incidentbot didn't page oncall for cluster-43 alerts between ~08:12-08:18 UTC. multiple customer reports. anyone seeing suppressor activity? :rotating_light:
ops-bot: [ALERT] paging-suppressor triggered for route=prod-pager due to duplicate-detection loop (6m). keeper-service returned 500 on checks, suppressor entered FAIL_OPEN -> suppressed pages.
sam: seeing a backlog of ~40 queued pages, delivery attempts to mobile gateway failed with 502s. ack-window errors spiking.
jess: I manually paged oncall-3 at ~08:20 to get eyes on customer impact. they confirmed receiving phone page and started mitigation.
mira: quick glance at keeper logs, looks like a config reload caused a transient panic and restart loop. keeper returned intermittent 500s which the suppressor interpreted as keeper unavailability and stopped outgoing pages.
sam: log snippet from suppressor (truncated):
```
ERROR handler.go:142 keeper-check failed status=500 body="panic: nil pointer"
stack: goroutine 56 [running]: keeper.Service.Check(...)
```
sam: rollout candidate ready to skip the faulty dedupe keeper check and force-pass health for 10m while we fix code. suggest bypass for immediate restore.
alex: I prefer bypassing short-term, but want controlled approach — canary then prod. jess, can you keep manual paging as backup until automated pages confirm delivery?
jess: yes, manual paging in place. also notified affected customers that we're working on infra-side paging.
sam: deploying canary now: `kubectl -n notify rollout restart deployment/incidentbot-suppressor --selector=canary=true`
deploy-bot: Canary started for deployment/incidentbot-suppressor in namespace notify at rev=sha256:7a9c. health checks are running.
deploy-bot: Canary health failed on readiness probe (502 -> /healthz) — rolling back canary.
mira: that's the flaky part. i'll roll keeper to new image that fixes nil deref and re-run canary with extended readiness.
alex: if canary fails again, fallback plan: flip suppressor into bypass-mode (config flag: `suppressor.strict=false`) and restart so pages flow, then iterate on keeper in parallel.
ops-bot: manual bypass applied by ops at 08:28 UTC (suppressor.strict=false). suppressor resumed forwarding pages; backlog processing started.
sam: forcing backlog flush: `notifyctl flush-backlog --route prod-pager` — submitted.
ops-bot: backlog flush succeeded, 42 pages delivered to mobile gateway between 08:29-08:33 UTC. delivery success rate improved to 99.2%.
oncall-3: Confirmed: received manual page and subsequent automated pages after bypass. no duplicate pages observed.
jess: customers we talked to saw restored notifications around 08:30 and acknowledged incident with support.
mira: I've promoted keeper patch to prod (rev sha256:8b2d) and restarted keeper pods. monitoring for error return-rate.
sam: rolling deploy completed, no further 500s observed in keeper checks for 8m.
alex: mitigation summary: 1) applied temporary bypass to suppressor, 2) flushed backlog, 3) patched keeper and redeployed, 4) validated deliveries and customer confirmations.
alex: creating incident ticket INC-2026-231 for postmortem, assigning to @sam and @mira for RCA and action items. will schedule retro tomorrow.
mira: I'll add a follow-up to tighten dedupe window logic and fail-open telemetry so suppressor doesn't misclassify transient keeper errors as long-term unavailability.
sam: adding a metric alert on keeper-500-rate > 1/min so we get paged before suppressor trips.
ops-bot: paging automated routes resumed and stable at 08:34 UTC.
alex: thanks everyone — closing live coordination here. please continue updates in INC-2026-231 and add any customer impact notes. :thumbsup:
